title: The Miracles of Jesus
description: Water into wine, a nobleman's dying son, a net about to break, a paralysed man lowered through a roof, a storm told to be still, a little girl raised, bread for five thousand, a walk on the sea, ten lepers and a blind beggar. The miracles of Jesus told from the King James Bible, and what each one shows us about who he is, ending in prayer.

beats.say: The gospels call them signs. Not tricks to impress a crowd, but signposts, each one pointing past itself to the person who did it.
And many other signs truly did Jesus. But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
So as we watch each miracle tonight, ask the question the disciples asked in the boat: What manner of man is this?
A village wedding in Cana of Galilee, a feast that would last for days. And halfway through, the unthinkable: the wine ran out.
His mother came to him: They have no wine. Then she said to the servants: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. Still good advice.
Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them up to the brim. Six stone jars, more than a hundred gallons, filled by hand from the well.
Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast. He tasted, and called the bridegroom: thou hast kept the good wine until now.
This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory. His first sign was not in a temple. It was at a party, sparing a family's shame.
A nobleman from Capernaum walked a full day to find Jesus. His son was at the point of death. Sir, come down ere my child die.
Jesus did not go with him. He said: Go thy way; thy son liveth. And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way.
On the road home his servants met him. Thy son liveth. When did he begin to mend? Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him. The very hour Jesus spoke.
He had to walk home on nothing but a promise. Sometimes that is what faith is: walking away from the place of prayer, before you see a thing, because he said so.
Simon had fished all night and caught nothing. He was washing his nets on the shore when Jesus stepped into his boat and asked him to push out a little.
Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught. Master, we have toiled all the night, and have taken nothing: nevertheless at thy word I will let down the net.
They enclosed a great multitude of fishes: and their net brake. They filled both ships, so that they began to sink.
Simon fell down at his knees: Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord. And Jesus said: Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
In Capernaum the house was so full that no one could reach the door. Four men arrived carrying a friend who could not walk.
So they went up on the roof, broke it open, and let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay, right in front of Jesus.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said: Son, thy sins be forgiven thee. The scribes were outraged: Who can forgive sins but God only? Exactly.
Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house. He rose, and walked out before them all, and they said: We never saw it on this fashion.
Evening on the Sea of Galilee. There arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And Jesus was asleep on a pillow.
They woke him: Master, carest thou not that we perish? The real fear under every storm: does he even care?
And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea: Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith? And they feared exceedingly: What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
Jairus, a ruler of the synagogue, fell at Jesus' feet: My little daughter lieth at the point of death. Jesus went with him, and the crowd pressed in.
On the way, a woman who had bled for twelve years touched his robe from behind. If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole. And straightway she was healed.
He stopped, and found her: Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace. But while he spoke, word came from Jairus's house: Thy daughter is dead.
Jesus said to the father: Be not afraid, only believe. He went into the room, took the child by the hand, and said: Talitha cumi; Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
And straightway the damsel arose, and walked. He told them to give her something to eat. The Lord of life, thinking about a hungry twelve year old.
Five thousand men, besides women and children, in a lonely place at the end of the day. Philip did the sums: two hundred pennyworth of bread would not be enough.
Andrew said: There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes: but what are they among so many?
Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to them that were set down. And every one ate as much as they would.
Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost. They filled twelve baskets with what was left over.
It began with a boy who gave everything he had, even though it was small. What feels too little in your hands may be exactly what he wants to bless.
After the crowd went home, he sent the disciples ahead by boat and went up a mountain alone to pray. By the fourth watch of the night, they were fighting the wind.
They saw a figure walking toward them on the sea, and cried out for fear. Straightway Jesus spake unto them: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
Peter said: Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said: Come. And Peter walked on the water.
But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried: Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him.
O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? He did not let go while he asked it. Little faith, caught by a strong hand, is still enough to walk back to the boat.
Ten lepers stood afar off, as the law demanded, and lifted up their voices: Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.
He told them: Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed. Healed on the way, not before they obeyed.
One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, and fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks. And he was a Samaritan.
Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole. Nine were healed. One was made whole. Gratitude made the difference.
Outside Jericho, a blind beggar named Bartimaeus heard the crowd pass and began to shout: Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.
Many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal. Some prayers are answered because they refuse to be quiet.
Jesus stood still. Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee. And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.
What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? Lord, that I might receive my sight. Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole. And he followed Jesus in the way.
Let us pray. Lord Jesus, you turned water into wine, and calmed the sea, and raised a little girl by the hand. Nothing I bring you tonight is too large for you.
And nothing is too small. You cared about a wedding, a meal, and a child who needed lunch. I bring you the big things and the little ones.
Like Bartimaeus, I will not be quiet. Like the nobleman, I will trust your word on the road home. Like Peter, when I sink, I will cry: Lord, save me.
All things are possible to him that believeth. Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief. And whatever you choose to do, let me come back, like the one leper, and say thank you. Amen.
